story: Two things that Rust does better than C++
text: There's a misunderstanding in this comparison between Rust's trait object system and C++'s virtual functions. While both mechanisms allow for polymorphism, they are fundamentally different. Rust's trait system is a compile-time mechanism that allows expressing shared behavior between types, whereas C++'s virtual functions are based on runtime polymorphism and dynamic dispatch. I understand what "dyn" does here, but this is comparing apples to oranges. It would be more useful to explore the tradeoffs of these two systems and tips for going from one to the other rather than being stupid* and thinking this is a competition. * Yes, stupid. [VIDEO]
